Job Summary

The Director of Advancement Analytics and Insights is a high-level strategist responsible for designing, deploying, and leading comprehensive business intelligence and analytics functions within University Advancement. This role serves as the primary architect of data-driven fundraising frameworks at San José State University, turning complex data into actionable insights, delivering dashboards, forecasting, and strategic analysis that guide leadership and teams across the division.

The Director oversees a comprehensive philanthropy analytics strategy to support fundraising performance, engagement metrics, and campaign success, and data-informed decision-making across the division. The incumbent acts as a critical bridge between data structure (Advancement IT), data collection (Gifts and Records Administration), and data application (Prospect Research and Management, Development, Alumni Engagement), successfully championing a culture of data literacy, evidence-informed engagement, and proactive analytics across University Advancement.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the multi-year roadmap for advancement analytics, aligning data initiatives with philanthropic and engagement pipelines, university campaigns, and divisional priorities and performance goals
Serve as the division’s lead business intelligence analyst, leveraging data-driven insights to inform decision-making, identify opportunities, and drive strategic initiatives across departments
Partners with teams on division-wide data operations, guiding divisional staff, partners, and vendors to ensure consistent, high-quality analytical standards in accordance with CASE, AASP, and industry best practices
Design, implement, and standardize key performance indicators (KPIs), performance dashboards, and accountability frameworks for University Advancement teams and leadership
Design, build, and continuously optimize a comprehensive institutional suite of interactive dashboards, reports, and data outputs that track philanthropic productivity, pipeline velocity, and fundraiser production
Oversee the delivery of automated and self-service analytics reports to front-line gift officers and academic leaders, ensuring visual and data consistency
Translate highly complex multivariate data sets and data science configurations into clear, narrative-driven business insights tailored for non-technical internal users and foundation boards
Develop, deploy, and validate advanced predictive algorithms and statistical models (e.g., donor propensity, major gift affinity, and lifetime value modeling) to uncover untapped donor capacity
Build data-driven revenue projection and multi-year forecasting models to determine target objectives and track pipeline gaps
Integrate external wealth screening and relationship mapping data directly into automated internal scoring models

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Ability to communicate with constituents in a professional and respectful manner
Working knowledge of, or the ability to develop proficiency in, the appropriate and ethical use of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), in higher education and administrative contexts
Ability to apply emerging technologies to support operational effectiveness, data-informed decision-making, and service delivery to students, faculty, and staff
Demonstrated ability to support continuous improvement and organizational learning through the responsible application of technology within assigned areas of responsibility
Deep knowledge of predictive modeling, data mining, multivariate regression, and fundraising forecasting techniques within a higher education environment
Mastery of visualization software (specifically Microsoft Power BI) and the ability to construct secure, scalable row-level security dashboard architectures
Comprehensive knowledge of relational database structures and workflows inside complex advancement CRMs (such as Salesforce, Blackbaud CRM/NXT, Affinaquest, or Ellucian)
Strong understanding of CASE Reporting Standards and AASP data metric models
Superior capability to synthesize complex data matrices into narrative presentations and clear policy recommendations for university leadership
Ability to apply emerging technologies to support operational effectiveness, data-informed decision-making, and service delivery to students, faculty, and staff
Demonstrated ability to support continuous improvement and organizational learning through the responsible application of technology within assigned areas of responsibility
Ability to evaluate potential applications, promote responsible, ethical, and equitable use, and ensure alignment with institutional policies, regulatory requirements, and strategic priorities
Demonstrated ability to manage multi-phase analytics projects independently under tight deadlines while successfully driving tool adoption among resistant users
Exceptional judgment regarding donor data privacy laws (FERPA, GDPR, CCPA) and an uncompromised commitment to professional ethics

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in Data Science, Business Intelligence, Statistics, Computer Science, Economics, or a related field
Five (5) years of progressively responsible professional experience in data analysis, business intelligence, or institutional analytics
Experience leading large-scale analytics initiatives or acting as a primary system analyst/strategist in a complex institutional or corporate environment

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree or higher in Data Science, Analytics, Business Administration (MBA), or an equivalent field
Seven (7) or more years of experience in higher education advancement services, prospect development analytics, or public university foundation data systems
Experience with fundraising principles and methods
Direct experience supporting multi-million fundraising initiatives using predictive fundraising pipelines
Experience with the California State University system, auxiliary organization models, and campus data compliance standards
Experience with SQL for data extraction, Python or R for statistical data modeling, and experience utilizing generative AI plugins for prompt engineering and rapid analytics

Morgan Stanley Community Development Finance is seeking a senior-level Affordable Housing Finance Product Manager to lead the end-to-end management of the Firm’s affordable housing private equity investment portfolio. The role will oversee the full investment lifecycle—from sourcing and origination through underwriting, transaction approval, closing, portfolio and asset management, governance, risk monitoring, performance reporting, and investment exits.

This individual will serve as a senior product owner and relationship manager for affordable housing private equity strategies, working closely with internal stakeholders, fund managers, sponsors, legal counsel, risk partners, and other control functions to ensure disciplined execution, strong portfolio performance, and alignment with Morgan Stanley’s community development, risk management, and business objectives.

Note: Location is open within the the U.S.

Oversee the affordable housing private equity product strategy and portfolio management framework, including origination priorities, investment guidelines, portfolio objectives, performance targets, and exit planning.
Lead sourcing and originations for new affordable housing private equity investment opportunities, including evaluation of fund managers, sponsors, markets, investment structures, projected returns, community development impact, and strategic fit.
Oversee due diligence, underwriting, financial analysis, market review, sponsor and guarantor assessment, legal documentation, and transaction approval materials for new investments and follow-on commitments.
Present investment opportunities, portfolio updates, risk matters, and strategic recommendations to transaction council, senior management, credit partners, and other internal governance forums.
Serve as the primary relationship manager for affordable housing private equity fund managers, developers, sponsors, and other external partners, ensuring strong communication, accountability, and execution.
Manage post-closing portfolio oversight, periodic asset reviews, compliance monitoring, operating performance analysis, capital account tracking, distribution forecasting, valuation support, and watchlist management.
Monitor fund and underlying asset performance against underwriting expectations, investment agreements, regulatory requirements, and CRA objectives.
Represent Morgan Stanley on fund advisory boards, investor committees, and other governance bodies, providing guidance on consents, amendments, waivers, workouts, dispositions, and other material portfolio matters.
Partner with internal risk stake holders to ensure appropriate controls, approvals, reporting, and issue resolution.
Lead, mentor, and develop staff supporting affordable housing private equity products, promoting strong execution standards, analytical rigor, and consistent portfolio management practices.

Skills Required

Deep understanding of affordable housing finance, private equity fund structures, LIHTC investments, multi-family real estate underwriting, asset management, and portfolio risk management.
Strong financial modeling, valuation, credit analysis, cash flow forecasting, and investment performance assessment skills.
Proven ability to evaluate complex transactions, identify risks, develop mitigation strategies, and make sound investment recommendations.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex investment, risk, and portfolio matters clearly to senior management and governance committees.
Strong relationship management and negotiation skills with demonstrated ability to work effectively with fund managers, developers, sponsors, legal counsel, and internal control partners.
Highly organized, detail-oriented, and able to manage multiple priorities, transactions, portfolio matters, and deadlines in a complex institutional environment.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word; experience with portfolio reporting systems, investment databases, and data visualization tools preferred.

Experience

15+ years of relevant experience in affordable housing finance, private equity, multi-family real estate investment, asset management, credit, or portfolio management.
Demonstrated experience managing investments across the full lifecycle, including origination, underwriting, approval, closing, construction or stabilization monitoring, ongoing asset management, workouts or restructurings, and exits.
Experience with public sector financing sources and regulatory frameworks, including Low-Income Housing Tax Credits, HUD/FHA programs, tax-exempt bonds, state and local housing programs, and other community development tools.
Established relationships with affordable housing developers, fund managers, lenders, investors, public agencies, and other industry participants preferred.
Prior experience leading teams, managing senior stakeholder relationships, and operating within a regulated financial institution or similarly complex investment platform strongly preferred.

Position Summary

Based in Shelburne, Vermont, Community Heart & Soul is seeking a Chief Operating Officer (COO) to serve as the organization's senior internal operating executive. Reporting directly to the President, the COO leads day-to-day operations, staff coordination, financial management support, and organizational infrastructure—enabling the President to remain fully focused on national expansion, partnership development, and strategic growth.

This is a significant leadership opportunity at a compelling moment. Community foundations, statewide philanthropic networks, and civic organizations are key in the growth of Community Heart & Soul's resident-led program. The COO will play a central role in ensuring that this national growth is matched by strong systems, disciplined execution, and a thriving internal culture—without veering into mission-creep. The COO upholds the organization's commitment to its core identity as it scales.

This is an in-office position based in Shelburne, VT. Some travel is required to meet with partners, Heart & Soul communities, and attend conferences and events. 

Primary Responsibilities

Organizational Operations:

The COO ensures that Community Heart & Soul runs smoothly, efficiently, and professionally every day.
Oversee day-to-day operations and translate approved strategic priorities into clear, actionable work plans.
Coordinate internal systems across all departments and monitor progress against projects and deadlines.
Identify opportunities to improve workflows, meeting rhythms, reporting systems, and decision-making processes.
Ensure staff have the tools, information, and support needed to do their best work.
Maintain operational momentum and continuity as the organization grows—especially when the President is traveling or externally engaged.

Staff Leadership and Culture

The COO strengthens accountability while preserving Community Heart & Soul's collaborative culture and mission-centered spirit.
Provide day-to-day management that supports staff and sustains a healthy, highperforming team environment.
Coach managers and staff through operational challenges; support performance management and professional development.
Foster collaboration across the program, communications, market development, finance, and administrative functions.
Preserve the current spirit of trust, flexibility, and shared mission as the organization evolves.

Financial and Business Operations

Lead annual budgeting and ongoing budget monitoring in partnership with the Finance Director and President
Translate budget decisions into operating plans; review operational expenses and identify efficiencies.
Support the Finance Director in preparing the annual audit.
Manage contracts, MOUs, vendor relationships, and purchasing processes.
Ensure financial information is consistently available to inform planning and decisionmaking.

Risk Management and Compliance

The COO ensures the organization minimizes its risk exposure and protects its assets.
Oversee risk management across contracts, human resources, intellectual property, and organizational compliance.
Ensure that personnel policies are current, clearly communicated, and consistently applied.
Oversee benefits administration, HR compliance, and accurate administrative recordkeeping.
Ensure the organization renews and enforces its trademark protection, domain names (URLs), and other brand-related assets.

Human Resources and Administration

Lead hiring, onboarding, and staff transitions; coordinate performance review processes.
Support staff development and internal communication to build a strong, capable team.
Help ensure the organization is appropriately staffed for current and future needs.

Oversee internal technology systems and vendor relationships, including database, CRM, file management, and knowledge management platforms.
Support cybersecurity, data integrity, and technology planning.
Help the organization use technology to improve efficiency, accountability, and partner follow-through.

Partnership and Growth Support

The COO ensures that the organization's national growth is operationally supported and sustainably managed.
Ensure partnership commitments are tracked, fulfilled, and supported by strong internal systems including MOU’s and Seed Grant tracking.
Coordinate internal readiness for conferences, partner gatherings, and national presentations.
Build scalable systems that allow the organization to grow without outpacing internal capacity.
Help ensure that expanding visibility and demand are met with operational excellence.

Board and Governance Support

The COO supports the President in preparing for Board meetings, committee work, and governance-related follow-through.
Support preparation of Board materials and track follow-up from Board and leadership meetings.
Help ensure organizational reports are timely, accurate, and useful for governance.
Support governance calendars, annual planning, and policy updates.

Vice President of Programs
Vice President of Communications
Market Development leadership
Finance Director

The ideal candidate brings senior operational leadership experience and a proven track record of building strong internal systems within mission-driven organizations. Qualifications

Senior operational leadership experience in a business or nonprofit mission-driven organizations.
Demonstrated success managing people, systems, budgets, vendors, and complex projects.
Strong business judgment and financial acumen.
Experience supporting an externally-facing executive in a growth-oriented organization.
Comfort operating within a board-influenced environment.

Develop and apply grant-acceptance and partner-vetting policies, escalating edge cases through the appropriate governance channels.

Advanced degrees or a scientific/clinical background required.
5+ years of progressive experience in partnerships, innovative programming, grants, including relationship ownership.
Demonstrated success building and diversifying non-dues or grants revenue and converting transactional sponsorships into multi-year partnerships.
International/global experience and cultural fluency.
Fluency in healthcare funder and industry relations and the compliance environment governing industry–society relationships.
Experience building teams, systems, and pipelines from an early state.
Exceptional relationship-building, negotiation, and written/verbal communication skills.
